title: Preserve Unicode arguments in Windows replay launchers
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

A valid Windows verifier command containing 6,000 Greek characters succeeds directly, but the replay gate expands it from 6,072 to 37,064 UTF-16 units and fails with WinError 206 before verification starts. Preserve Unicode in the JSON command transport at both the registered gate and isolated-test supervisor. The repaired gate uses 7,064 units and preserves the complete argument vector.

Only two JSON serialization options change in production. Job ownership, startup isolation, deadlines, bytecode isolation, completion receipts and cleanup keep their existing behavior. This is a portability repair; no mathematical certificate, immutable source pin or selected κ changes.

[Evidence, reproduction, attribution and limits](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fb6df7db6a3253aa39a54f6aecdc3bcdb99fa971/docs/research/windows-unicode-replay-argv.md).

## Task and overlap

Task `portable-replay`, refined to one native launch failure, priority revision 7; chooser nonce `b7847175b3ee9e8ce9f110910afc833a`. [Canonical claim/completion record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1472#discussioncomment-19140347).

Started at canonical main `f259dabc7d70e0db8d6d36bfda888f008bbfecc1`; refreshed and rebased onto `5948b8770d5f6df94d70a9f8ec6c0759586f592c`, retaining PR5017's separate worker-exception repair. Submission overlap covered 303 open PRs, 4,152 Discussion records and all 6,754 tracked local notes. The focused Unicode/JSON query found only this claim; arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain outside coverage. The earlier sparse-baseline pathspec batching and Windows lifetime repairs address different boundaries.

## Validation

Native Windows 11 build 26300, AMD64 CPython 3.12.0, standard library:

```sh
python -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_windows_unicode_argv.py -v
python -O -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_windows_unicode_argv.py -v
python -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_windows_job.py -v
python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_isolated_test_*.py' -v
```

- New tests: **6 pass** in each mode, including BMP/supplementary Unicode, exact mixed-character round trips and nonzero status.
- Before the repair: six WinError 206 outcomes across five methods; the short positive control passes.
- Separately restoring ASCII escaping in either layer makes the optimized tests fail again.
- Existing Job Object suite: **8 pass**. Existing isolated-runner suite after rebase: **42 pass, 8 Linux-only skips**.
- Committed bytes match all four working files; `git diff --check` passes. AST comparison against refreshed main confirms only the two JSON options change in the production scripts.

The newly merged `test_research_worker_failure_order.py` has a separate Windows LF-only output expectation at line 69: one pass, one failure, six POSIX-only skips. The identical CRLF/LF failure reproduces with six unchanged-main files in a fresh temporary fixture. Its expected bytes are not changed here.

No archive-wide registered replay, selected cold replay, new Linux/macOS/newer-Python execution or independent human review is claimed. Hosted checks are separate from these local results.

## Credit

Retains ywz65's gated Job Object and startup-isolation work; Mihir Srivastava's isolated supervisor; Nick Petalas and Paul Romeo's lifetime controls; Aaron Wang/navinor's scheduler; Douglas Colkitt and the retained runner contributors. Prepared for Mihir Srivastava (@mihir-s-05) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, one agent; Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Commands near the native limit can still exceed it after wrapper overhead or quote/backslash escaping. A private-file/pipe transport would require a separate observed case and ownership/cleanup review. This PR removes the demonstrated non-ASCII expansion only. The inherited Windows newline fixture failure is documented for a separate repair.
